note: Set A binds the tile, wallboard, gable and bracket facts cleanly and captures the detail scales (D1/D3/D5 at 6"=1'-0", D5 at 1 1/2"=1'-0"), the 3/8" porcelain wall tile, lot number and project name, with quotes that match the text. Set B adds the 1/4" per foot substrate slope that A misses, but it fabricates the quote "3\" SUBFLOOR FIN." to invent a 3 in subfloor thickness, misbinds P3 (a finish on the MDF gable) as part of the L-bracket attachment, calls THIN SET the top layer, and treats the layer name FIN. BATHROOM FLOOR as a finish value, plus it omits the porcelain wall tile and all detail scales and repeats several claims. A's only real defect is the vague PT1 'surface finish' claim, so A is the stronger set overall.
